content: Ozanimod, a medication that inhibits monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) in vitro, has the potential to cause serious adverse reactions, including hypertensive crisis. Therefore, it is not recommended to co-administer ozanimod with drugs that increase norepinephrine or serotonin levels. When ozanimod is used with methylprednisolone, the immunosuppressive effects of both drugs may be enhanced, increasing the risk of infection. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Similarly, co-administration with other immunosuppressive therapies may lead to additive immune effects during treatment and in the weeks following administration.
